Set Sail for Success
Sunday Times State Primary School of the Year | Ofsted Outstanding
What makes us special?
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to our website. Whether you are an existing family or visiting us for the first time, I hope this site gives you a clear sense of what makes Mayflower School such a vibrant, welcoming place to learn and grow.
Having been part of the Mayflower community for 18 years—including over a decade as Deputy Headteacher—it is an absolute privilege to now lead our school as Headteacher. Having served this community for so long, I know first hand the incredible potential of our pupils, the dedication of our staff, and the strength of our partnership with families. Our school takes its name from The Mayflower, the famous ship that carried early pioneers on a historic journey. That pioneering spirit continues to inspire everything we do as we strive for excellence. We are constantly searching for innovative ways to make learning exciting, so that every pupil enjoys the sense of adventure that education brings and discovers how learning changes lives.
As our pupils 'Set Sail for Success', my commitment is to build on our strong foundation and ensure Mayflower remains an ambitious, safe, and joyful environment where every child is empowered to thrive.
I look forward to continuing our journey together.
Adam Stock, Headteacher
Leaders in Learning
See some of our scientifically research backed projects aimed at giving your children the best start in life
Have a seat...
We are leaders in new techniques for learning. One of our new techniques is allowing children to choose a seat. This allows children to concentrate because they don’t have to be uncomfortable.
Learning Through Storytelling
We are leaders in new techniques for learning. One of our new techniques is 'learning through storytelling'. We have found that all humans connect through storytelling, and so we feel it’s the best way to educate pupils.

PE and Sport Premium
At Mayflower we believe that engaging in a range of physical activities is essential to our pupils’ well being.
The yearly grant from the government has enabled us to continue to deliver high quality PE, Sports and Dance. This grant is partly used to fund our SLA with the Tower Hamlets Youth Sport Foundation.

Breakfast Club
We want every child at Mayflower Primary School to start the day with a healthy, filling breakfast.
Children can arrive any time between 8.00 am and 8.40 am they will be offered a selection of healthy breakfast options: a variety of cereals, porridge oats, boiled eggs, beans, bagels, juice and milk. A great way to start the day!
We do not charge for breakfast club and our breakfast club benefits from the support of the Magic Breakfast Mayor's Fund for London Project. We also have bagels to share at break time too!

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - Mayflower Primary School
pageCache.text:
Set sail for success
Modern Foreign Languages
At Mayflower, learning a foreign language is more than just acquiring a skill—it's a window into new cultures and perspectives. We are proud to teach Spanish, a language that ignites curiosity and deepens our pupils' understanding of the diverse world around them.
Our engaging Spanish curriculum, spanning KS2, brings language learning to life. Through vibrant songs, playful rhymes, and a carefully crafted programme of study, we inspire pupils to explore new ways of thinking and communicating. Lessons are designed to help children express their ideas, understand and respond to others and use language for real-world purposes.
While Spanish is our focus, our teaching also lays a strong foundation for future language learning, equipping pupils with skills that will ease their transition to secondary school and beyond.
Our Goals for Pupils:
At Mayflower, Spanish isn't just a subject—it’s a journey into global citizenship, encouraging our pupils to embrace the richness of the world with curiosity and confidence.

pageCache.pageTitle: Physical Education (PE) at Mayflower - Mayflower Primary School
pageCache.text:
Set sail for success
Physical Education (PE) at Mayflower
At Mayflower our mission is to increase children’s positive attitude towards PE and sports. We aim to give all of our pupils the opportunity to keep active and develop an enjoyment in physical activities. We recognise that our curriculum needs to provide opportunities for pupils to become physically confident in ways that support their health and fitness. Encouraging children to develop a positive mind-set in PE is essential in combatting the obesity crisis in our country. Not only is it good for their physical and mental health, but it also helps to instil and embed values such as respect and fairness through competition.
Our aim is for all pupils to:
Our pupils take part in 2 hours of PE each week - for our classes in LKS2, this includes an hour of swimming. We have a street dance specialist that teaches across all year groups throughout the year and helps to provide our pupils with body confidence and poise. In addition to this, weekly ‘Sensory Circuits’ sessions for EYFS and KS1 provide a range of activities to develop children’s core strength and gross/fine motor skills.
Our children are offered the chance to take part in a variety of after school sports clubs such as football and dance. These clubs are led by skilled members of staff and sports coaches who help support the children grow in confidence and ability.

pageCache.pageTitle: RE at Mayflower - Mayflower Primary School
pageCache.text:
Set sail for success
RE at Mayflower
At Mayflower, we believe RE gives us the opportunity to find commonality between the world’s major religions. We aim for our pupils to leave the school having developed as compassionate, thoughtful and confident individuals with an in-depth knowledge of a range of world religions.
In RE, our pupils learn about different religions, world views and ways of life in local, national and global contexts. They discover, explore and consider many different answers to questions about human identity, meaning and value. We teach RE using a cross-curricular approach often weaving storytelling, drama, art or history into topics.
Through our annual interfaith week we meet representatives from each major religion (as well as humanism). This event gives our pupils the opportunity to understand the links and mutual respect that exists between different religions. Our pupils also have the opportunity to visit a range of different places of worship such as Neasden Temple, The Buddhist centre in Bethnal Green and the local Roman Catholic Church.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music at Mayflower - Mayflower Primary School
pageCache.text:
Set sail for success
Music at Mayflower
At Mayflower, Music is a vital part of our curriculum where pupils have the opportunity to develop their creativity, confidence and collaborative skills.
In Nursery and Reception, Music weaves itself through many areas of discrete and indiscrete learning. Research shows us that 'early childhood settings are full of rich and spontaneous music-making' (Music Mark) and at Mayflower, this is no exception. Music can be observed through: pupils vocalising within their water play; playing rhythmically with bricks as they build; creating sound effects to accompany their play with vehicles and animals; singing short phrases in their role play (Music Mark). EYFS pupils at Mayflower sing daily Nursery Rhymes and use various songs to help them understand educational and social concepts. Exposing pupils to Music of different cultures is also an important part of celebrating the diverse mix of families in our school. Pupils are encouraged to actively listen to their surroundings - helping them to develop aural skills - which later transfers to phonological awareness. Reception pupils at Mayflower also perform a nativity musical each December.
From Year 1 onwards, Music is taught using the Sing Up Curriculum. In KS1, the focus is on developing the following key elements: singing and listening, composing, musicianship (beat, rhythm and pitch). In LKS2 the focus expands to include improvisation, performance and reading notation. In KS2, pupils develop their performance and instrumental skills. All Music lessons are taught by the class teacher and are based around pupils listening, responding to and being inspired by contemporary and historical music from around the world.
Pupils from Reception to Year 6 have the opportunity to play the djembe drum in termly blocks with a specialist tutor. Pupils in Year 5 learn to play either the flute, clarinet or ukulele. We regularly hold after-school Music clubs, which have involved playing recorder, keyboard, rap club, choir and exploring Music Technology.
We are passionate about giving our pupils the opportunity to perform both within and outside of school. Each year the school takes part in a range of projects with professional musicians. These often involve performing at local venues and with other schools. Recent projects have included working with the LSO, Maroon Town, Restore the Music, Spitalfields Music, Barbican, English Touring Opera and Be the Band.
